title: POC: script compatibility + fallthrough routing scoping
summary: Align on POC success criteria for benchmark integration: validate customer scripts with Redwood harness, define streaming vs non-streaming acceptance, size workload and throughput targets, and agree on timeline and next steps for a two-week pilot with telemetry hooks and security review.
topics: customer harness adapter and script compatibility
action_items: Maya Chen: Share benchmark template + sample harness adapter repo (due 2027-06-07)
Omar Singh: Run initial compatibility check with customer's sample script and report failures (due 2027-06-09)
Priya Kapoor: Provide 3 representative request traces and token distributions (due 2027-06-06)
Sara Levin: Circulate SOC2/Audit questions and required encryption notes (due 2027-06-08)
next_steps: Redwood to deliver sample adapter and benchmarking spreadsheet by 2027-06-07
Customer to provide request traces and sample prompts by 2027-06-06
Follow-up deep dive scheduled 2027-06-10 to review first harness run
Set up short-lived Dedicated pilot if baseline throughput shows >2x improvement over current infra
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, really appreciate it. quick roll call? 
00:07 Priya Kapoor: Priya here, platform lead at BlueNova. hello. 
00:10 Ethan Morales: Ethan, ml engineer. tiny voice, hi. 
00:12 Sara Levin: Sara from security. hi. 
00:14 Omar Singh: Omar Singh, Solutions Engineer, Redwood. glad to be here. 
00:18 Maya Chen: Cool. agenda — we want to scope the POC for benchmark harness integration, confirm success criteria, and decide streaming vs nonstreaming harness approach, also timeline. is that right priya? 
00:27 Priya Kapoor: yeah that's perfect. our main thing is we need to know if our existing inference scripts can plug into Redwood's harness without too much rewrites and we need firm latency/throughput numbers for our SLA decision. 
00:38 Omar Singh: yep, perfect. quick FYI — our harness supports two modes: a streaming client adapter that replays token stream and a batched non-streaming runner that sends full prompt and waits. both have different telemetry hooks and different tradeoffs for tail latency. 
00:52 Ethan Morales: quick question — our scripts rely on partial response scoring, we do token-level scoring we can't really batch because we need stream callbacks. so streaming is more realistic for our workload. 
01:05 Omar Singh: that's fine. streaming is the typical path for partial scoring. we need to see your client library though — sometimes the http streaming semantics differ and our adapter needs a small shim. often it's a 15-40 line shim but can be larger if you do custom chunking. 
01:22 Priya Kapoor: what about throughput? we expect about 80 concurrent sessions at peak with an average of 150 tokens per session and peak qps around 12. can you ballpark required capacity? 
01:36 Maya Chen: ok, so 80 concurrent sessions * 150 tokens — that's about 12k tokens in-flight. with streaming we think a single Redwood Dedicated slab (nv8x?) could handle X — (note: exact model/kernel choice will affect this) — omar, want to call out our initial estimate? 
01:53 Omar Singh: right. rough baseline: assuming a 4-bit quantized model variant we commonly onboard, per-GPU sustained token throughput is about 10k-30k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and kernel choices. for your profile, I'd estimate 1-2 GPUs for baseline, but the harness run will confirm. also tail latency and cold-starts matter — if you do many short sessions there's overhead. 
02:15 Ethan Morales: are those numbers for the current model we use? we're on a 7B replica fine-tuned model, not a 70B. 
02:22 Omar Singh: yes 7B-ish numbers. for larger models numbers drop; for 70B you'd need different planning. 
02:29 Priya Kapoor: we also use KV cache reuse across sessions sometimes, does Redwood support prefix caching across pooled requests? we don't want to resend the same system prompt repeatedly. 
02:38 Omar Singh: yes, prefix/KV caching is supported — we can configure your workload to reuse cache between sessions when safe; that often reduces per-request token compute by 15-40%. we'll want to see your session patterns to tune TTLs. 
02:53 Sara Levin: security question — if we go Dedicated, what's the KMS story? do we manage keys or do you? and audit logs? 
03:00 Maya Chen: good callout. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. we can also provide audit logs to your SIEM; we'll share our security package after this call. 
03:12 Sara Levin: and data residency? our logs need to stay within EU for some data. 
03:16 Maya Chen: we have region pinning — Private deployments are required for strict residency; Dedicated in specific cloud regions can also meet that. we'll map that in the security doc. 
03:26 Priya Kapoor: success criteria — what do you think we should define as acceptance? for us it's: 1) compatibility with our client scripts without major rework, 2) streaming latency under 200ms 95p for interactive flows, 3) cost per 1M tokens below our threshold, and 4) no PII leaks and SOC2 level auditability. 
03:48 Omar Singh: that aligns. we usually ask for a small benchmark: you give us three representative request traces, we run them in streaming and batched modes in the harness, and we produce a report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, cost estimates, and an itemized compatibility log. pass criteria could be your 95p <200ms and functional parity for callbacks. 
04:12 Ethan Morales: what about tokenization differences? our tokenizer is a slightly modified bpe and sometimes token counts differ. how do you handle that in comparisons? 
04:21 Omar Singh: we'll bring your tokenizer into the harness — adapter supports custom tokenizers and we log tokenization deltas. you should provide a small tokenization test set. that will be one of the first action items. 
04:32 Priya Kapoor: timeline? we are hoping to move quickly — pilot in two weeks, full pilot for 2-3 weeks, then decision. is that realistic? 
04:41 Maya Chen: yes, realistic if we get artifacts quickly. propose: Day 0-3 customer shares traces, sample scripts, and a small model bundle if possible; Day 4-7 Redwood does adapter and first harness run; Day 8 sync to fix failures; Day 9-14 full swept runs and cost modelling. follow-up 1:1 on day 7. 
04:58 Priya Kapoor: ok. action items are clear. 
05:01 Sara Levin: one more security nuance — we cannot have logs that include raw prompts unless redaction is applied. can you support prompt redaction in telemetry? 
05:09 Omar Singh: yes, redaction hooks exist; we can redact or hash prompt text in telemetry and still preserve length and token distribution stats. we'll show the redaction pipeline. 
05:22 Ethan Morales: about fallback routing — our app wants graceful degradation to a smaller quantized model when capacity hits a threshold. can Redwood switch variants transparently? 
05:31 Omar Singh: absolutely. we support policy-based routing: at request-time, rules can route to cheaper quantized variants, fallback to region or lower-tier model. we preserve KV cache where compatible and provide a confidence tag in the response so the app can adjust. 
05:46 Priya Kapoor: are there risks with QA if model variant changes mid-session? 
05:50 Omar Singh: yes, that's why we recommend canaries: route a small percent to the variant and run a quality regression on a fixed eval prompt set. quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize can alert you on drift. 
06:04 Maya Chen: let's talk about the harness adapter specifics — our team will send a sample of your client script. we usually provide a python shim and a node shim. the shim maps your callback hooks to Redwood stream events. common mismatch: customers do chunk-level ack that doesn't line up with our chunk framing, so we add a re-chunker. 
06:26 Ethan Morales: our script has mid-response inserts based on external DB calls which slow the stream — will that break the harness? 
06:33 Omar Singh: the harness can simulate backpressure. we can instrument the shim to replay the inserts asynchronously or simulate latency. we record per-chunk latency so you can see if your DB calls cause tail spikes. 
06:46 Priya Kapoor: can you produce a benchmarking spreadsheet with cost calculations and GPU sizing assumptions? 
06:51 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a workbook that shows tokens/sec, estimated GPUs required, and cost sensitivity across quantization levels. expect that as part of the sample artifacts. 
06:59 Ethan Morales: one technical detail — streaming vs non-streaming differences in token accounting and cost: do you charge on token emitted or on compute tokens? 
07:08 Omar Singh: we charge by tokens processed for inference; emitted tokens and input tokens both count — streaming doesn't change the token accounting but it can affect latency and batching efficiency which indirectly affects effective tokens/sec and cost. we'll show both rows in the spreadsheet. 
07:23 Priya Kapoor: what's your SLO for p95 latency? we want to compare to our current in-house SLO. 
07:28 Maya Chen: hosted SLOs are 200ms p95 for small-gen models; Dedicated can be configured tighter depending on reserved capacity and model selection. we'll add SLO targets to the proposal. 
07:40 Sara Levin: regarding compliance, do you support SAML SSO for the console and RBAC for team members? 
07:45 Maya Chen: yes, SAML and SCIM for provisioning plus fine-grained RBAC. Dedicated adds SSO enforcement and audit retention controls. 
07:54 Ethan Morales: on the harness run, will we get raw audio or just logs? (laugh) — jk, just logs. will you provide trace IDs across request lifecycle? 
08:02 Omar Singh: yes, we produce trace IDs and per-token timing breakdowns and a downloadable CSV of raw telemetry. 
08:10 Priya Kapoor: ok. on scoring — we need to ensure that partial scoring (our case) lines up with stream chunk boundaries, else scores could be off. how do you recommend we validate scoring parity? 
08:22 Omar Singh: we'll run a parity test: run your scoring function against raw stream captures locally and compare to the harness outputs with the same chunking. mismatches will be flagged in the compatibility report with suggested shim changes. 
08:37 Maya Chen: Anything else on integrations? 
08:39 Ethan Morales: edge-case: we occasionally send variable-length system prompts up to 2k tokens that are common across sessions; can the cache handle large prefixes? 
08:47 Omar Singh: yes, but cache sizing and TTL will be part of the tuning plan — very large prefixes can reduce effective cache hit if sessions vary. we'll recommend heuristics. 
08:58 Priya Kapoor: are there known gotchas for our infra? we use a mix of on-prem and cloud, with a proxy that terminates TLS and does request multiplexing. does Redwood handle proxied connections? 
09:09 Maya Chen: yes, we've seen similar setups. for headless proxies we provide a tokenized handshake and keepalive settings recommendations. sometimes multiplexers change connection semantics for streaming; that is usually the small shim we discussed. 
09:27 Sara Levin: are there any legal procurement steps we should plan for? template terms or data processing addendum? 
09:33 Maya Chen: we'll send a standard DPA and an enterprise terms deck. procurement typically wants a 2-3 week review; we can parallelize security review and bench runs. 
09:43 Priya Kapoor: sounds good. next steps recap? 
09:46 Maya Chen: I'll list them — Redwood shares benchmark template, shim repo, security pack; BlueNova shares token traces, sample script, and SOC questions; Omar runs initial compatibility, we sync on 2027-06-10. any objections? 
09:59 Priya Kapoor: none. 
10:01 Ethan Morales: no objections. 
10:04 Sara Levin: fine. thanks everyone. 
10:07 Maya Chen: great — we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts. thanks, bye. 
10:12 [call ended] 

Notes on ASR: occasional mishearings — "nv8x" transcribed as "N V 8 X", "KV cache" as "K V cache", and some product names like "Redwood Optimize" might appear as "Redwood opti-mize". There were short cross-talk segments and filler words that were left in. This transcript is lightly cleaned but retains timestamps and typical speaker attribution inconsistencies.
